methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Science CLIL Integration
content: Problem: Students often know basic vocabulary but struggle to explain scientific concepts using logical reasoning and full sentences.

Solution: We explicitly teach the grammar of reasoning ("because") integrated with the science content (characteristics of life). Students don't just say "It's living"; they must argue "It is living because it breathes and grows."

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the core characteristics of living things (breathe, grow, move). Focus on basic classification.
Session 2: Practice classifying tricky items (e.g., plants, water, robots). Use "because" and "does not".
Session 3: Full production. Write an explanatory paragraph classifying objects and present the findings orally.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a flashcard of an object. The student must classify it and give one reason (e.g., "A rock is non-living because it does not grow.").

Communicative task (Step 5 - 10 min): The Sorting Game. Pairs of students receive a stack of picture cards and must ask each other questions to sort them into "Living" and "Non-Living" piles with spoken reasons.

content: All living things can grow, breathe, eat, move, and reproduce.

Yesterday, Detective Max went to the park. He investigated many objects.
First, he found a little green frog. "The frog is a living thing," Max wrote in his journal. "It is living because it breathes air, moves by jumping, and grows bigger."
Next, he saw a big brown bench. "The bench is a non-living thing," he wrote. "It is non-living because it does not need food. It does not grow."
After that, Max looked at the river. "Water moves, but is it living?" he thought. "No, water is non-living because it does not breathe or have babies."
Max learned that we must observe carefully to find the truth!

Welcome to my final science presentation! I am Detective Luna.

Today I will explain the rules of nature. There are many different things in our world. We divide them into living and non-living things. How do we know the difference? It is easy if you observe carefully!
A living thing is special because it breathes, grows, and moves. It also needs food and water to survive. For example, a cat is a living thing. A tree is a living thing too!
But a plastic chair is a non-living thing. It is non-living because it does not breathe and it does not grow.
You can be a nature detective too! Just look around your house and classify what you see. Science is everywhere!

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The Detective's Journal
content: All living things can grow, breathe, eat, move, and reproduce.
A tree is alive — it grows from a seed, makes its own food, and produces new seeds.

Yesterday, Detective Max went to the park. He investigated many objects.

Next, he saw a big brown bench. "The bench is a non-living thing," he wrote. "It is non-living because it does not need food. It does not grow."
After that, Max looked at the river. "Water moves, but is it living?" he thought. "No, water is non-living because it does not breathe or have babies."
Max learned that we must observe carefully to find the truth!

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: "because" for scientific reasoning
instructions: Grammar focus this week: "because" for scientific reasoning.

Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

listening_script.text: Hello, scientists! Today we are investigating living and non-living things. A dog is a living thing because it breathes, grows, and moves. A rock is a non-living thing because it cannot breathe or grow. A flower is living because it needs water and sunlight to grow. A toy car is non-living because it cannot breathe or move by itself. Remember: we use 'because' to give scientific reasons. Now listen again and check your answers on your worksheet.

listening_script.text: Good morning, young scientists! I will now present my life investigation report. I investigated four objects: a cat, a pencil, a plant, and a stone. The cat is living because it breathes, moves, and grows. The pencil is non-living because it cannot breathe, move, or grow by itself. The plant is living because it grows toward the sun and needs water. The stone is non-living because it has none of the seven signs of life. My conclusion: living things breathe, grow, and move because they have life energy.
